questions.question_text: Find the total of $1.8\text{ kg}$ and $450\text{ g}$.

options.why: Treats 450 grams as 0.045 kilogram instead of 0.45 kilogram.
Adds the numbers without first converting them to a common unit.
Moves the decimal in 450 grams incorrectly before adding.

questions.question_text:
A $4.2\text{ kg}$ container loses $650\text{ g}$.
What mass remains?

options.why: Treats 650 grams as 0.065 kilogram before subtracting.
Subtracts 0.55 kilogram rather than the given 0.65 kilogram.
Subtracts 1.9 kilograms through an incorrect unit conversion.

questions.question_text: How much heavier is $2.6\text{ kg}$ than $2450\text{ g}$?

options.why: Loses a place value when subtracting 2450 grams from 2600 grams.
Subtracts 2350 grams rather than the stated 2450 grams.
Adds the masses instead of finding how much heavier one is.

questions.question_text:
Five packs each have mass $320\text{ g}$.
What is their total mass in kilograms?

options.why: Divides the 1600-gram total by 10000 instead of 1000.
Adds the number of packs to the mass instead of multiplying.
Converts the gram total using the wrong place-value shift.

questions.question_text:
A trailer limit is $1.5\text{ t}$.
It carries $860\text{ kg}$ of soil and $675\text{ kg}$ of stone.
By how much does it exceed the limit?

options.why: Subtracts only the stone mass from the limit and ignores part of the load.
Finds the total load but does not subtract the allowed limit.
Converts 0.035 tonnes to kilograms using only one decimal-place shift.

questions.solution_text:
$1.5\text{ t}=1500\text{ kg}$
$860\text{ kg}+675\text{ kg}$
$=1535\text{ kg}$
$1535\text{ kg}-1500\text{ kg}$
$=35\text{ kg}$

questions.question_text:
A baker has $6\text{ kg}$ of dough and makes $14$ loaves of $380\text{ g}$ each.
How much dough remains?

options.why: Finds the mass used but reports it instead of the amount remaining.
Subtracts 380 grams only once from 6 kilograms.
Uses 370 grams per loaf instead of the stated 380 grams.

questions.solution_text:
$14\times380\text{ g}$
$=5320\text{ g}$
$6\text{ kg}=6000\text{ g}$
$6000\text{ g}-5320\text{ g}$
$=680\text{ g}$

questions.question_text:
Amanda is sending these parcels.
Their masses are $350\text{g}$, $0.5\text{kg}$, and $4\text{kg}$.
The cost is £3.00 per kilogram.
How much will Amanda have to pay in total?

options.why: The parcel masses have not been correctly combined before applying the rate.
The 350g parcel has been treated as 35kg instead of 0.35kg.
The 350g parcel has been treated as 350kg instead of 0.35kg.

questions.solution_text: Convert $350\text{g}=0.35\text{kg}$. The total mass is $0.35+0.5+4=4.85\text{kg}$. The cost is $4.85\times£3.00=£14.55$.
